chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated from his father, from Abi Sa'id al-Adamy, from al-Hasan ibn al-Husayn al-Lu'lu'i, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Ziyad, from Abi Abdillah, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever wishes to increase the good in his house, let him wash his hand before eating.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of washing hands before eating according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) linking physical cleanliness to spiritual abundance, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *taharah* (purity) as a gateway to divine mercy. This practice is not merely hygienic but is viewed as a means of preserving the *barakah* (blessing) of sustenance within the domestic sphere, aligning bodily discipline with spiritual mindfulness.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-90 Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar - may God be pleased with him - narrated that his father quoted on the authority of Abi Sa’id al-Adamy, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn al-Hussein al-Lu’lu’ee, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sa’id ibn Qazvan, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Abi Zyad, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), on the authority of his father (MGB), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB) that the Commander of the Faithful Imam Ali (MGB) said, “Whoever wants to increase the good in his house should wash his hands before he eats.”
